newsitem.title: USA: Travelers' Weill had stock option gain.
newsitem.headline: Travelers' Weill had stock option gain.

text.p: Travelers Group Inc Chairman Sandy Weill in 1996 realized $85 million through stock appreciation and the exercise of options that were granted 10 years ago, and also earned $8.7 million in compensation for the year, Travelers Group spokeswoman Mary McDermott told Reuters.
"He did not have $94 million in earnings," McDermott said.
She said Weill's salary was $1.05 million, plus a cash bonus of $5 million and a restricted stock award of $2.6 million. Weill's salary has been unchanged for the past three years, McDermott said.
The bonus rose by 16 percent, and the total compensation was about 13 percent higher than in 1995.
She said that in addition to the compensation, "In the course of the year he exercised options that stemmed back to an original grant that was made in 1986."

Robert Lipp, chairman, chief executive and president of Travelers Property Casualty Corp, received compensation of $4.7 million, McDermott said. This included salary of $600,000, a cash bonus of $2.7 million and a restricted stock award of $1.4 million.
Travelers Property Casualty is an 82-percent owned subsidiary of Travelers Group. ((--Hartford newsroom (860) 727-0224))
